nodeData.note: The CFE is a professional credential for people who find, investigate and stop fraud. It is awarded by the Association of Certified Fraud Examiners (ACFE). This map covers what it is, who can sit it, the exam, and how Kenyan accountants and auditors use it.

children.topic: What it is and why it matters
children.note: Start here: what the letters mean, who awards them, and why an accountant would want them.
CFE means Certified Fraud Examiner. It shows you have been tested on how fraud happens, how to investigate it and how to prevent it.

manas.q: What does CFE stand for and what does it show?

children.topic: The body behind it: the ACFE
children.note: The Association of Certified Fraud Examiners, based in Austin, Texas, USA. Joseph T. Wells founded it in 1988. It trains people and publishes material on fraud.

manas.q: Who awards the CFE, and who founded that body?

children.note: The ACFE has given out the CFE credential since 1989, one year after the association began.

manas.q: Since when has the CFE been awarded?

children.note: Collects evidence, studies records, interviews people, writes a clear report on what happened, and helps the business close the gap so it does not happen again.
Auditors, accountants, bank and SACCO staff, risk and compliance officers, investigators and anyone whose job touches fraud. A degree in any field can count towards entry.
The ACFE regularly publishes a study of real fraud cases called the Report to the Nations. Look up the latest edition for current figures; this map does not quote them.
The "Forensic accounting" map (Branches) explains the wider field, and the CA24 and CA34S2 auditing maps cover the auditor's duties on fraud. This map stays on the CFE itself.
A few simple ideas sit under the whole CFE syllabus. Learn these before the exam details.
Fraud is deliberately tricking someone to take money, property or a right from them, or to gain unfairly. The key word is deliberate: an honest error is not fraud.

manas.q: What is fraud, in one line?

children.note: Fraud done by a person against the organisation they work for, using their job to do it. Example: a cashier pocketing takings.

manas.q: What is occupational fraud?

children.note: The ACFE sorts occupational fraud into three families: stealing or misusing assets, corruption, and fiddling the financial statements.
Taking cash, stock or other things the business owns. Examples: skimming cash sales, ghost employees, fake supplier invoices.

manas.q: What is asset misappropriation? Give two examples.

children.note: Misusing influence in a deal for personal gain. Examples: bribes, kickbacks from a supplier, hidden conflicts of interest.

manas.q: What counts as corruption in the fraud tree?

children.note: Making the accounts look better or worse than the truth on purpose, e.g. booking fake sales or hiding expenses.

manas.q: What is financial statement fraud?

children.note: A simple model of why ordinary people commit fraud. It grew from the research of criminologist Donald R. Cressey. Three things are usually present together.
A need or push, such as debts, school fees, a gambling habit or targets that feel impossible.

manas.q: Fraud triangle: what is pressure?

children.note: A gap that lets the fraud happen and stay hidden, usually weak internal controls, e.g. one person both receives and banks cash.

manas.q: Fraud triangle: what is opportunity?

children.note: The story the person tells themselves to feel okay: "I will pay it back", "They underpay me anyway".

manas.q: Fraud triangle: what is rationalisation?

children.note: A business cannot remove staff pressure, but it can shrink opportunity with good controls. Taking away one side lowers the risk.
Deterrence removes the reasons and chances for fraud so people do not try. Prevention spots and stops fraud attempts. The CFE exam tests both.

manas.q: What is the difference between fraud deterrence and prevention?

children.topic: Who can become a CFE: five steps
children.note: The ACFE sets five requirements. You can sit the exam before you meet all of them.

manas.q: What membership do you need before the CFE?

manas.q: How many eligibility points to sit the exam, and to be certified?

children.note: Two years of fraud-related professional work can stand in for each year of study. Example: 2 years of college (20 points) plus 4 more years of experience. (check acfe.com for the current rules, checked 27 Nov 2026)

manas.q: How can experience replace a degree for CFE points?

children.note: By the time you are certified you need at least two years of work linked to detecting or deterring fraud. Accounting and auditing work are accepted categories. (check acfe.com for the current rules, checked 27 Nov 2026)

manas.q: How much experience is needed, and by when?

children.topic: You can sit the exam first
children.note: The two years of experience are needed at certification, not before the exam. So a young auditor can pass early and certify later.
All three sections must be passed. See the next branch for details.

children.topic: 5. Agree to the Code of Ethics
children.note: You must agree to follow the ACFE Code of Professional Ethics. (check acfe.com for the current rules, checked 27 Nov 2026)

manas.q: What is the fifth CFE requirement?

children.note: Three separate timed exams. Multiple-choice and true/false questions only, and you may not use any reference material. (check acfe.com for the current rules, checked 27 Nov 2026)

manas.q: CFE Section 1: name, time and number of questions?

children.note: Fraud Investigations and Legal Issues: 2.5 hours, 120 questions. Covers investigations, evidence, interviews, report writing, common-law and civil-law systems, and expert testimony. (check acfe.com for the current rules, checked 27 Nov 2026)

manas.q: CFE Section 2: name, time and number of questions?

children.note: Fraud Prevention and Deterrence: 1.5 hours, 70 questions. Covers why people commit fraud, corporate governance, fraud risk assessment, prevention programmes and ethics. (check acfe.com for the current rules, checked 27 Nov 2026)

manas.q: CFE Section 3: name, time and number of questions?

children.note: 120 + 120 + 70 = 310 questions. 2.5 + 2.5 + 1.5 = 6.5 hours of exam time.

manas.q: Total questions and hours in the CFE Exam?

children.note: One option is online with a remote proctor (someone watching by camera) through Prometric ProProctor. Other formats also exist. (check acfe.com for the current rules, checked 27 Nov 2026)

manas.q: What is the CFE pass mark?

Each annual period you need at least 20 continuing professional education (CPE) credits. (check acfe.com for the current rules, checked 27 Nov 2026)

Real-style cases with KES numbers. Business names are invented.
Tumaini Hardware Ltd pays its staff by bank transfer. The auditor compares the payroll to the HR list of real staff.
March payroll: 42 names, KES 2,100,000. HR list of real staff: 40 people, KES 2,010,000. Gap: 2 names x KES 45,000 = KES 90,000.
Both extra names are paid into the same bank account as a payroll clerk. Nobody on the HR list knows them.
The names appear for 6 months: 6 x KES 90,000 = KES 540,000 paid to people who do not exist.
Dr Amount due from employee (or fraud loss) KES 540,000 / Cr Salaries and wages KES 540,000. Salaries were overstated, so the cost moves out.
Separate the person who adds staff to payroll from the person who approves payment, and reconcile payroll to HR every month.
At Baraka Mini-Mart, the till sales for sugar look low. The examiner compares stock movement with cash sales.
2 kg sugar: opening 200 packets + bought 500 − closing count 150 = 550 packets sold.
550 x KES 300 = KES 165,000 expected. Till shows KES 135,000. Gap KES 30,000, which is 100 packets.
Sales of about 100 packets were not rung up, a sign of skimming: cash taken before it enters the books. Next, check till shifts and who was on duty.
A gap can also come from theft of stock, breakage or wrong counts. Gather evidence first; an examiner reports facts, not guesses.

Section 1: 150 minutes / 120 questions = 1.25 minutes, about 75 seconds each. Section 3: 90 / 70 = about 77 seconds each.
12 hours fraud webinars + 2 hours ethics + 6 hours tax update = 20 credits. Fraud 12 (≥ 10) and ethics 2 (≥ 2), so it meets the rule.

nodeData.note: The CFA (Chartered Financial Analyst) is a global qualification for people who analyse investments and manage money. This map explains the three levels, who can enrol, costs, what you study, and a few worked investment sums in KES.

children.topic: What it is and why it matters
children.note: The CFA is for investment work: valuing shares and bonds, building portfolios and giving sound, ethical advice. It is run by CFA Institute, a US-based not-for-profit body.
CFA means Chartered Financial Analyst. Someone who finishes the programme and meets the other rules is called a CFA charterholder.

manas.q: What does CFA stand for, and what is a charterholder?

children.topic: The body behind it: CFA Institute
children.note: CFA Institute is an American not-for-profit professional body. Wikipedia says it was formerly called the Association for Investment Management and Research (AIMR).

manas.q: Which body runs the CFA Program?

children.note: Accounting qualifications teach how to record and report. The CFA teaches how to use those reports to judge what an investment is worth.
CFA Institute says there are more than 200,000 charterholders worldwide. (check cfainstitute.org, checked 27 Nov 2026)
Wikipedia says successful candidates take about four years on average to earn the charter. It is a long road, so plan for it.
Accountants and finance graduates who want to work in fund management, stockbroking, banks, pension schemes, insurers or investment research.
Three levels, each with its own exam. Pass all three, gain work experience and join CFA Institute to become a charterholder.
The CFA Program has three levels and you sit one exam per level, in order: Level I, then II, then III.

manas.q: How many levels and exams are in the CFA Program?

children.note: CFA Institute's guide is about 300 hours of study for each level, so roughly 900 hours in total. (check cfainstitute.org, checked 27 Nov 2026)

manas.q: How many study hours per level does CFA Institute suggest?

children.note: 1) Pass Levels I, II and III. 2) Get qualifying work experience. 3) Become a regular member of CFA Institute. 4) Then you may use the CFA designation.

manas.q: What do you need to become a CFA charterholder?

children.note: You document 4,000 hours of investment work experience. The work must be in, or add value to, investment decision-making. (check cfainstitute.org, checked 27 Nov 2026)

manas.q: How much work experience does the charter need?

children.note: The work experience can be gained before, during or after you take the exams.
When applying for membership you submit 2–3 professional references. (check cfainstitute.org, checked 27 Nov 2026)
Enrol → Level I → Level II → Level III → experience and references → member → charterholder.
You need ONE of three things: a degree, to be close to finishing a degree, or enough work and/or study hours. (check cfainstitute.org, checked 27 Nov 2026)
If you already hold a bachelor's degree, you can enrol.

manas.q: Name the three ways to qualify to enrol in the CFA Program.

children.note: An undergraduate may enrol if their Level I exam window is 23 months or less before graduation.

manas.q: How close to graduation must a student be to sit Level I?

children.note: Level II must be within 11 months of graduation. For Level III you need the degree finished or 4,000 hours of experience.
4,000 hours of work experience and/or higher education over at least three sequential years. A year of higher education counts as 1,000 hours.

manas.q: What is the work-and-education route to enrol?

children.topic: That work need not be investment
children.note: For enrolment, the work does not have to be investment-related, and paid internships count.
Enrolment route 3 accepts any work or study. The charter's 4,000 hours must be investment work. Different rules.
Dates and fees from cfainstitute.org, checked 27 Nov 2026. They change, so check before you register.
Exams run four times a year, usually February, May, August and November, in more than 400 locations. Not every level is in every window. (check cfainstitute.org, checked 27 Nov 2026)

manas.q: How often are CFA exams offered, and in which months?

children.note: You can sit a CFA exam at most twice in one calendar year, never in back-to-back windows or windows within six months of each other.

manas.q: What is the limit on CFA exam attempts per year?

Wanjiru buys 1,000 shares of an NSE-listed company at KES 40.00 each, gets a dividend of KES 2.00 per share, and sells a year later at KES 46.00.
Holding-period return = (selling price − buying price + income) ÷ buying price.

manas.q: What is the formula for holding-period return?

children.note: Cost 40,000. Price gain 6,000 + dividends 2,000 = KES 8,000. 8,000 ÷ 40,000 = 20%. Same answer.

children.topic: Present value of a coupon bond
children.note: A KES 100,000 bond pays a 10% coupon (KES 10,000) at the end of each year for 3 years, then repays the face value. Investors want 12%.
Price = each future payment ÷ (1 + yield) raised to the number of years, all added up.

manas.q: How do you price a bond?

children.note: 8,928.57 + 7,971.94 + 78,295.83 = KES 95,196.34. The bond sells below face value (at a discount).
If investors wanted 10%, the same sums give exactly KES 100,000. Yield = coupon means price = face value.

manas.q: What happens to a bond's price when the yield rises above the coupon rate?

children.note: A SACCO invests KES 500,000: KES 300,000 (60%) in shares returning 15% and KES 200,000 (40%) in bonds returning 10%.
Portfolio return = sum of (weight × return) for each asset.

manas.q: How do you work out a portfolio's return?

children.note: Shares earn 45,000 and bonds 20,000, total KES 65,000. 65,000 ÷ 500,000 = 13%.
A company earns KES 5.00 per share (EPS). Similar listed companies trade at 8 times earnings. Its share price today is KES 36.00.
P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. It shows how many shillings investors pay for each shilling of yearly profit.

manas.q: What is the P/E ratio?

children.note: 5.00 × 8 = KES 40.00 per share.
Its own P/E is 36.00 ÷ 5.00 = 7.2, below the peers' 8. On this test it looks cheap, but check why first.

nodeData.note: A university degree and the CPA are two different things that work well together. This map helps a school-leaver or parent compare routes: degree, CPA, diploma first, or both, and plan time and money.

children.topic: What it is and why it matters
children.note: A degree is an academic award from a university. The CPA is a professional exam from KASNEB. Many accountants in Kenya end up with both.
A university course, usually about four years, where you study business with a focus on accounting. In Kenya this is often a Bachelor of Commerce with an accounting option.

manas.q: What is an accounting degree, in simple words?

children.note: BCom means Bachelor of Commerce. It is a first degree covering accounting, economics, finance and management, mostly offered in Commonwealth countries.

manas.q: What does BCom stand for, and what does it cover?

children.note: A degree gives broad knowledge and a university award. A professional exam like the CPA tests the skills employers and the profession expect of an accountant.

manas.q: How is a degree different from a professional qualification like the CPA?

children.note: Both cost money and years. Choosing the right order saves fees, time and stress, and helps the student start earning sooner.
A Kenyan form four leaver, or a parent, deciding between a degree, the CPA, a diploma first, or a mix.
The Commission for University Education (CUE) is the government body that regulates universities and their courses in Kenya.
CUE regulates and accredits universities and the programmes they teach. It was set up by the Universities Act No. 42 of 2012 (check the current rules, checked 27 Nov 2026).

manas.q: What does the Commission for University Education (CUE) do?

children.note: CUE took over from the Commission for Higher Education, which had existed since 1985.

manas.q: Which body did CUE replace, and since when had it existed?

children.note: CUE keeps a public list showing the status of each university. Look your chosen university up here before you apply.
CUE also lists the academic programmes offered in Kenyan universities. The course itself must be on it, not just the university.

manas.q: Besides the university, what else must be accredited by CUE?

children.note: If you study abroad or online with a foreign university, CUE has a process to recognise and equate that qualification in Kenya (check the current rules, checked 27 Nov 2026).

manas.q: Which CUE service handles degrees earned outside Kenya?

children.note: CUE posts public advisories, for example about campuses and qualifications. Read them before choosing a campus.
KUCCPS handles placement of government-sponsored students into universities and colleges. Its site is kuccps.net. Self-sponsored students usually apply to the university directly.

manas.q: What does KUCCPS do?

children.note: Always check that BOTH the university AND the programme are accredited on the CUE site before paying any fees.

manas.q: What must you check on CUE before paying university fees?

children.topic: What you study in the degree
children.note: Most accounting degrees share a core of business subjects, then an accounting or finance option in later years. Exact units differ by university.
Recording transactions and preparing financial statements: what the business owns (assets), owes (liabilities) and earns (income).
Working out what things cost and helping managers plan, budget and decide.
How income tax, VAT and other taxes work for people and businesses, with Kenyan rules.
Checking whether financial statements are fair and controls work.
How markets, prices, money and the wider economy behave.
Contracts, companies, agency and other laws that affect business.
Maths and statistics for business: percentages, interest, data and probability.
Spreadsheets, accounting packages and basic data skills. Employers expect these.
Many courses include a work attachment. It is often the first real taste of the job and a source of references.
There is no single right path. These are common routes Kenyan students take.
A general commerce degree where you choose accounting (or finance) in later years. The most common route.

manas.q: What is the most common degree route into accounting in Kenya?

children.note: A management degree that can include accounting units. Broader, with less accounting depth.
Do a diploma (for example a KASNEB diploma or a college diploma), work, then join a degree later. Good if grades or money are tight now.
Study the degree and sit CPA papers in parallel. Hard work, but you can finish both soon after graduating.
Finish the degree, then do the CPA. Graduates can apply for exemptions from some papers.
Go straight into the CPA with a KCSE C+ (Plus). Cheaper and faster to a professional exam, but no degree.
A Master's (for example in finance or accounting) after some work. Useful for teaching, research or senior roles.
The CPA is KASNEB's professional accounting exam. It sits beside a degree; it does not replace it, and a degree does not replace it.
KASNEB accepts a KCSE mean grade C+ (Plus), a KASNEB diploma, another recognised diploma, or a bachelor's degree from a recognised university (check the current rules, checked 27 Nov 2026).

manas.q: What are the entry requirements for the KASNEB CPA?

children.note: The current CPA has Foundation (CA511–CA516), Intermediate (CA521–CA526), Advanced (CA531–CA536) and Post-advanced (CA537P–CA539WP) (check the current rules, checked 27 Nov 2026).

manas.q: What are the four levels of the current KASNEB CPA?

children.note: CA511 Financial Accounting, CA512 Management and Communication, CA513 Business Law and Ethics, CA514 Economics, CA515 Quantitative Analysis, CA516 Digital Accounting.
CA521 Public Finance, CA522 Financial Management, CA523 Financial Reporting and Analysis, CA524 Audit and Assurance, CA525 Management Accounting, CA526 Taxation.
CA537P Business Data Analytics, CA538WE Workshop on Ethics, and CA539WP Work Experience/Work Simulation Workshop.

manas.q: What are the three post-advanced CPA requirements?

children.note: Many degree units (financial accounting, economics, law, tax, audit) cover similar ground to CPA papers. That is why doing both is common.
Graduates can apply to KASNEB for exemptions from some papers; check the current exemption list on kasneb.or.ke (check the current rules, checked 27 Nov 2026).

manas.q: Can degree holders get CPA exemptions, and where do you check?

children.note: Three different things: a university degree, the KASNEB exam, and ICPAK membership.
ICPAK is the professional body for certified public accountants in Kenya, set up under the Accountants Act No. 15 of 2008 (check the current rules, checked 27 Nov 2026).

manas.q: What is ICPAK and under which law was it set up?

children.note: ICPAK is a member of the International Federation of Accountants (IFAC) and the Pan African Federation of Accountants (PAFA).

manas.q: Which international and regional bodies is ICPAK a member of?

children.topic: A degree alone is not a CPA
children.note: Graduating in accounting does not make you a CPA. You must pass the professional exams and meet the professional body's requirements.

manas.q: Does an accounting degree alone make you a CPA?

children.note: University (accredited by CUE) awards the degree. KASNEB sets and runs the CPA exam. ICPAK is the professional body for CPAs.
Many accounting job adverts in Kenya ask for a degree plus CPA, or CPA plus experience. Read real adverts for the job you want.

children.topic: Payback: how long to earn it back
children.note: If the degree costs KES 480,000 and lifts pay by KES 20,000 a month, payback = 480,000 ÷ 20,000 = 24 months. Illustration only: invented round numbers, not real fees.

manas.q: How do you work out the payback period on study costs?

children.note: CPA cost KES 250,000; extra pay KES 25,000 a month. Payback = 250,000 ÷ 25,000 = 10 months. Illustration only: invented round numbers, not real fees.

children.topic: Return on study in one year
children.note: Extra pay KES 20,000 × 12 = KES 240,000 a year on a KES 480,000 cost. Return = 240,000 ÷ 480,000 = 50% a year. Illustration only: invented round numbers, not real fees.

manas.q: How do you work out a simple yearly return on study?

children.note: To save KES 120,000 for next year's fees in 12 months: 120,000 ÷ 12 = KES 10,000 a month.

children.topic: If grades are C+ or above
children.note: You can enter a degree (subject to the university's own rules) or go straight into the CPA. Many do both.
Consider CPA first or a diploma first, live at home, and work while studying. Ask the university about loans and bursaries.

children.topic: If you want banks, NGOs or abroad
children.note: A degree plus a professional exam opens more doors. For study abroad, check CUE recognition of foreign degrees.

children.topic: If you want to start work fast
children.note: CPA or diploma first gets you into an accounts office sooner; the degree can come later, part time.

Payback = cost ÷ extra pay per month.
